key_insight: Exact boundary and initial constraints enable PINNs to identify the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 accurately from sparse, noisy simulated wavefields.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support nondestructive characterization of shear electromechanical coupling in PMUTs and SAW devices without dedicated destructive resonance tests.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers into network outputs to enforce boundary and initial conditions exactly.
Train against coupled electro-elastodynamic equations and sparse observations, eliminating boundary and initial-condition penalty weights.
Nondimensionalize governing coefficients to comparable scales for optimization.
evidence_signal: Across six formulations on manufactured data at 30 dB, constrained PINNs achieved 0.15–0.51% mean e15 error; the full formulation achieved 1.19% on finite-element data sampled along one subsurface line.
watch_item: Validation uses simulated plane-strain data; robustness to experimental noise, model mismatch, and real device geometries remains unestablished.
paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
